subject: 🤖 DeepSeek V4-Flash beats V4-Pro on 9 benchmarks, same size
intro: The real story today isn't bigger models. It's better training . DeepSeek's V4-Flash just beat its own flagship Pro on agent benchmarks, same size, just retrained. Alibaba's Qwen3.8-Max codes autonomously for 10 days straight. And a new paper shows a simple for-loop boosts image generation efficiency 6x. We're watching post-training become the new moat. Raw parameters matter less every week.

news.headline: DeepSeek launches V4-Flash API with stronger agent skills and Codex support
news.body: DeepSeek just pushed V4-Flash into public beta , and the story here is not a bigger model. Same architecture, same size as the preview. They just retrained it, and the numbers jumped hard. The agent scores now beat the higher-tier V4-Pro-Preview across all nine benchmarks. We're talking about a lighter model outrunning its own bigger sibling on real coding tasks: To use it, just set your model to deepseek-v4-flash . No URL changes, no auth changes. If you were already calling this endpoint, you got the upgrade automatically. Note: scores are vendor-reported, not independently verified yet. V4-Pro API and the web app are still unchanged.
bullets: Terminal Bench 2.1: 82.7 vs 72.1 for V4-Pro-Preview, nearly matching Anthropic's Opus-4.8 at 85.0
Native Responses API support plus full Codex integration, out of the box

news.headline: Open-source Rust tool classifies PDFs in 20ms, no OCR needed
news.body: PDFs have always been a pain for AI agents. You send one through OCR (a slow process that reads text from images), and you wait seconds per page. Firecrawl just shipped pdf-inspector to fix that. The trick: not every PDF needs OCR. About 54% of PDFs are already text-based, like reports, invoices, and research papers. pdf-inspector checks which type you have in roughly 20ms, then skips OCR entirely for text-based files and only sends scanned pages through the slow path. What you get out of it: You can drop it in with pip install pdf-inspector or npm install @firecrawl/pdf-inspector. It is fully open source under MIT.
bullets: Clean markdown with correct reading order, tables, and formulas preserved
200 PDFs processed in under 5 seconds , faster than every competing tool
Works in Python, Node.js, Rust, or the CLI
No external services, no GPU needed for text PDFs

news.headline: Qwen releases 2.4T parameter model that codes autonomously for 10+ days straight
news.body: Alibaba just dropped Qwen3.8-Max , a massive 2.4 trillion parameter model built to handle real, long-running tasks on its own. Think of parameters as the model's "brain cells" -- more means more capacity to reason and plan. Here's what makes it different from typical AI models: You can access it now via Alibaba Cloud's API. Pricing sits at $2/M input tokens and $6/M output, with cached input dropping to just $0.25/M. Open weights for Qwen3.8-Max and the smaller Qwen3.8-27B are coming next week.
bullets: It ran 10+ days of autonomous coding -- starting from an empty folder and shipping production code with zero hand-holding
It handles text, images, video, and documents all in one model -- and uses what it sees to check and fix its own work
It ran 500+ rounds of chip design optimization and a full year of e-commerce planning, all on its own
API-compatible with both OpenAI and Anthropic protocols, so you can point existing tooling at it without a rewrite
